extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for reviewers evaluating submissions to the IJCAI 2025 conference, including procedures for Phase 1/Phase 2, rebuttals, conflicts, formatting violations, and use of tools like LLMs. Covers both evaluation criteria for papers and reviewer conduct requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 1 reviewing and early rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: In Phase 1, every paper will be reviewed by two reviewers and if a paper receives two reviews that are not sufficiently positive, it will be rejected without any opportunity to submit an author response. By submitting a paper, authors acknowledge that they are aware of the possibility of receiving a rejection notification after Phase 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 1 is a decisive early filter: two negative/insufficiently positive reviews lead to rejection with no rebuttal. Reviewers should be aware their Phase 1 evaluations may directly determine acceptance without further rounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback provided for Phase 1 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of papers rejected in Phase 1 will receive two reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reviews for Phase 1 rejections are constructive and informative because authors will receive them even though no rebuttal occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected level of paper quality
rubrics_metrics.description: IJCAI is the premier conference in AI; for fast-growing areas (NLP, vision, ML) a rule of thumb is to ask whether the paper is good enough for conferences such as ACL / ICCV / CVPR / NeurIPS / ICML / ICLR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these top conferences as comparative benchmarks when deciding whether a submission meets IJCAI standards; favor top-quality original research appropriate for a broad AI audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and permissible content of the rebuttal (author response)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the rebuttal is to ask questions about specific issues that (1) could directly influence your evaluation of the paper, and (2) do not require providing new results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical acceptable rebuttal questions: requests to clarify or justify particular issues, or about important relationships to other works. Unacceptable uses: asking for extra experiments or theoretical results, or engaging in a discussion about ways to extend or revise the paper. Reviewers must judge the current submission, not hypothetical future versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility of rebuttal and confidential comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal will be visible to all members of the program committee involved in the paper (PCs, SPCs, ACs, SACs, Associate PC Chairs, PC Chair). There is also the option to enter confidential comments that will not be visible to the reviewers, but will be accessible to the meta-reviewers, senior meta reviewers, and (associate) PC chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public rebuttal for points authors should address for reviewers; use confidential comments to communicate matters meant only for meta-reviewers/PC leadership (e.g., potential violations or sensitive concerns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of CFP rule violations (anonymity, length, formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers violating the rules specified in the CFP must be rejected. Most papers that obviously violated these requirements have been desk rejected before the reviewing phases. However, in case you find an obvious violation, please inform the workflow chairs (at workflow@2025.ijcai.org) immediately. You can also mention it in your review, though you must not take it into account in your judgment as decisions about violations are made by the PC-chair directly in order to ensure consistency and fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not incorporate formatting/anonymity violations into your scoring or acceptance rationale; report violations to workflow chairs and optionally note them in the review so leadership can act consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not attempt de-anonymization
rubrics_metrics.description: Please refrain from using search engines such as Google to try to identify the authors. This is not good practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid active deanonymization efforts; they compromise the double-blind process and are considered inappropriate reviewer behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find reviewer training and examples of good/bad reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Start by looking at the IJCAI review form. Recommended reading: 'Mistakes reviewers make' by Niklas Elmqvist and tutorial slides by Hendrik Blockeel and Jesse Davis adapted for IJCAI-ECAI 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New reviewers should consult the review form and the linked tutorial/articles to learn common pitfalls and expectations about tone, thoroughness, and structure of reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment rationale and what to do if the paper is outside your expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignment algorithm considers your bids, the subject areas, TPMS, as well as the reviewer workload, etc. It aims at optimizing the global assignment. If you did not bid, or entered positive bids for too few papers, or mainly on very popular papers, the algorithm may not have found the best papers for you. Still there are many other papers that need to be reviewed, and we rely on your expertise to provide an opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper does not at all match the subject areas entered for that paper, inform workflow@2025.ijcai.org and put it in your review (this is considered bad practice to accept completely mismatched assignments). If the paper is somewhat outside your core expertise, provide an informed-outsider evaluation; if you truly cannot provide a well-informed review (or have a COI), inform workflow immediately so reassignment can be attempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest and inability to review
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover a conflict of interest, or if you cannot review a paper for any other reason, inform workflow@2025.ijcai.org as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptly report COIs or inability to review; delays make reassignment harder. The same prompt reporting applies when you are unable to provide a well-informed review because of expertise mismatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on reviewing resubmissions (previously reviewed elsewhere / by you)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have reviewed a (re)submission for a previous conference, continue to review it. We don’t regard this situation as a COI. Reviewers for previous versions of the submission are in an ideal position to judge whether the current submission has been really improved. Note that submissions that have been rejected at any peer-reviewed conference within the past 12 months must declare the resubmission and attach the previous review as well as an explanation about how authors have improved the work. The resubmission file will be visible only after the rebuttal during the discussion period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not decline reviewing resubmissions based solely on prior knowledge; use your prior review to assess improvements. Expect to see the previous review and authors' explanation after rebuttal during discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria for application-focused papers
rubrics_metrics.description: IJCAI welcomes papers on AI techniques for novel application domains. If the use of AI, or the AI technique used, is novel for this kind of application, it can be considered, provided that the application is formalized in such a manner that the formalization can be applied to solve other applications in an innovative manner as well. If the paper doesn’t completely satisfy the previous criterion but it clearly explains why the used technique works well, again it can be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance depends on how important the application is, how significant the improvement is, and to which extent it can be generalized to other problems. If the paper doesn’t satisfy the previous criteria but the AI technique used has a major impact in the application domain and in industry or society, it may be considered for publication. Conversely, simply applying a standard AI/ML technique on standard datasets for an application does not constitute a valid contribution for IJCAI 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on prior non-archival appearances and preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary version of the paper has already appeared at arXiv, or been presented at a workshop or a conference without formal proceedings? That is not a problem as long as the papers are presented in non-archival venues (that is, as long as there are not formally published proceedings with a publisher, in general with a DOI, ISBN, or ISSN). ArXiv submissions are also ok.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat arXiv and non-archival workshop presentations as allowable prior dissemination; check declarations where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short paper / extended abstract policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No automatic rejection if the short paper is not longer than a two-column two-page paper. If the ‘short’ paper is longer than that, but no longer than half of the IJCAI paper, then the extension must be significant enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating papers with previous short/extended abstracts, check length thresholds and assess whether the current submission contains significant extension beyond the shorter version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted and prohibited uses of large language models (LLMs) in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: LLMs can only be used for polishing the reviewer-written reviews/meta-reviews, but not for other uses such as generation of opinions, assessment of strengths/weaknesses, judgments on the paper’s quality or significance, or recommendation of acceptance/rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers/meta-reviewers use an LLM in any part of the review/meta-review process, they assume full responsibility for all content, including checking for plagiarism and correctness of the entire review/meta-review. ACs, SACs and the Program Chair will monitor reviews for potential LLM misuse. Reviews/meta-reviews deemed irresponsible will be thoroughly investigated and will be dealt with very seriously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting PC chair and prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not find an answer to your question in the FAQ or CFP, you are welcome to contact the IJCAI-25 program chair at pcchair@2025.ijcai.org, but please make sure that you have read IJCAI-25 CFP and the current FAQ first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before emailing program leadership, consult the CFP and FAQ to avoid asking already-answered questions and to ensure efficient use of chair time.
